transcript.text: My Hotpoint washer dryer isn't drying properly any more and there's a funny smell when it's on the dry bit. Is there something I should clean?

Yes, the first thing worth cleaning is the pump filter at the bottom front of the machine, because fluff from drying collects there and a blocked filter can stop it drying properly. From what you have described, the most likely cause is the drying fan or air duct. Drying sends fluff and the condensed water out through the pump, so a clogged pump filter (bottom front) stops it drying and can make the condensed water back up and leak. Unplug it first and have towels and a shallow tray ready, then unscrew the filter slowly. Was the filter full of fluff or debris (and is it clean now), or was it already clean?
I haven't checked the filter yet. Should I do that first? Also worth saying the smell is like burning dust, and the top of the machine feels very hot when it's drying. I've kept using it so far.

⚠ Stop using this appliance
A burning or hot-plastic smell, smoke, scorching or melting can mean an electrical fault or a fire risk. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it (or turn it off at the fuse box), and don't run it again — not even as a test — until it has been checked by a qualified engineer. No, not as the first step. A burning-dust smell with the top of the machine getting very hot points to something an engineer should look at, so please stop using the drying cycle until then. From what you have checked, this needs an appliance engineer to look at it: the next steps are beyond the checks that are safe to do yourself.
